questions.q: Which three phases make up a marketing plan, according to the summary?
a: Before, during and after
Plan, build and launch
Research, pitch and close
Attract, engage and upsell
questions.why: The lessons split marketing into getting prospects, converting them, and looking after buyers.

a: A virtual avatar of your ideal customer
A list of everyone who has bought before
A script for your first sales call
A rival you benchmark your prices against
questions.why: Lesson 1 describes it as an avatar that thinks and acts like the customer you want to reach.

questions.q: What should you do right after a lead gives you their email address?
a: Follow up and introduce yourself
Send them a discount code that day
Add them to a public group chat
Wait a week before making contact
questions.why: Lesson 2 says that once you capture an email, you should follow up and introduce yourself.

questions.q: Why does the summary say a broken purchase link matters so much?
a: It wastes the money you already spent on marketing
It makes your brand look technically outdated
It lowers your ranking in search results
It lets rivals copy your offer quickly
questions.why: Lesson 2 compares dead links to throwing your whole ad budget out of the window.

questions.q: Which three factors decide whether a customer will buy from you again?
a: The product, the delivery and how it was received
The price, the packaging and the warranty
The ad, the website and the checkout
The brand, the reviews and the refund policy
questions.why: Lesson 3 names the product or service, the delivery process and the customer’s experience of it.
